title: Theorem
body_md: Let $(\mathcal M,\mathsf g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime with nonnegative timelike sectional curvature that contains a complete maximizing timelike geodesic $\Upsilon :\mathbb R \to \mathcal M$ (i.e., a complete timelike line). Then there exists a complete Riemannian manifold $(\mathcal S,\mathsf h)$ of nonnegative sectional curvature such that $(\mathcal M, \mathsf g) \cong (\mathbb R \times S, dt^2 - \mathsf h)$. In particular, $(\mathcal M,\mathsf g)$ is geodesically complete.
head: environment
name: Beem--Ehrlich--Markvorsen--Galloway

title: Theorem
body_md:
Fix $R > 0$. 
For every $\delta \ge 0$ and $L \gg R$,
there exists a quantity $\Psi = \Psi(\delta,L \, | R)$ with 
$\Psi(\delta,L \, | R) \to 0$ as $ (\delta,L^{-1}) \to 0$ 
such that the following holds: If $(\mathcal M,\mathsf g)$ is a globally hyperbolic spacetime with timelike sectional curvature bounded below by $-\delta \leq 0$ and $\Upsilon:[-L,L] \to \mathcal M$ is a maximizing timelike geodesic parametrized by Lorentzian arclength, then there exists a pointed metric space $(X,\mathsf d, x_0)$ (depending on $\delta,R,L,\Upsilon$ and $(\mathcal M,\mathsf g)$) such that
\begin{equation}
    \mathsf d_{LGH}(J^\mathcal M(\Upsilon_{-R},\Upsilon_R), J^{\mathbb R \times X}((-R,x_0),(R,x_0))) \leq \Psi(\delta,L\,|\,R)
\end{equation}
where $\mathsf d_{{LGH}}$ and the time-separation on $\mathbb R \times X$ are from Definitions 
\ref{D:d_LGH}--\ref{Definition: Lorentzian products} below.
head: environment
name: Almost-splitting under timelike sectional curvature bounds

title: Remark
body_md:
We shall eventually construct $X$ as the intersection of the diamond $J^{\mathcal M}(\Upsilon_{-R},\Upsilon_R)$ with the level set of $\ell(\Upsilon_{-L},\cdot)$ passing through $x_0 := \Upsilon_0$.  The monotonicity and semiconvexity \cite[Prop. 3.4]{McCann20} of 
$\ell(\Upsilon_{-L},\cdot)$ imply this level set is a locally Lipschitz (in fact DC \cite[Cor. 2.6]{KitagawaMcCann19}) 
spacelike hypersurface. Moreover, outside of the spacelike boundary $i^0$ of $J^{\mathcal M}(\Upsilon_{-R},\Upsilon_R)$ identified in Remark \ref{Remark: i^0} --- we expect the $DC$ implicit function theorem
\cite{VeselyZajicek89} to imply that
$X\setminus i^0$ is a locally $DC$ hypersurface-with-boundary on which the distance $\mathsf d$ we construct metrizes the discrete topology. Here $DC$ refers to manifolds in which the transition functions between charts are coordinatewise differences of convex functions; in particular,  such submanifolds are $C^2$-rectifiable.

label: eq: definition of concavity
title: Definition
body_md:
Let $(\mathcal M,\mathsf g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime and $C \subseteq \mathcal M$ be an open causally convex set. Given $\lambda \in \mathbb R$ we say that a function $f : C \rightarrow \mathbb R$ is \emph{causally $\lambda$-convex on $C$} provided, for all causal geodesics $\sigma : [0,1] \rightarrow C$ and for every $t \in [0,1]$, we have that
    \begin{equation} \label{eq: definition of concavity}    f(\sigma_t) \leq (1-t)f(\sigma_0) + tf(\sigma_1) - \frac{\lambda}{2} t(1-t) L_\mathsf g(\sigma)^2.
    \end{equation}
where we recall that $L_\mathsf g(\sigma)$ denotes the Lorentzian arclength of $\sigma$. Equivalently, the second derivative of $f$ satisfies $\frac{d^2}{dt^2} f( \sigma (t)) \geq \lambda L_{\mathsf g}(\sigma)^2$ in the distributional sense. A function $f:C \rightarrow \mathbb R$ is called \emph{causally $\lambda$-concave} if instead the reverse inequality holds in \eqref{eq: definition of concavity}.

title: Proof
body_md:
This is an immediate consequence of Theorem \ref{Theorem: Toponogov convexity version}, noting that the values of $\ell(\Upsilon_{-L},\cdot)$ and $\ell(\cdot,\Upsilon_L)$ are contained in the interval $(L - R, L + R)$ on $I(\Upsilon_{-R},\Upsilon_R)$. Thus, writing 
    \[
    f_\delta(t):=\mathrm{md}^{-\delta}(\ell(\Upsilon_{-L},\sigma_t))
    \]
    (or $f_\delta(t):=\mathrm{md}^{-\delta}(\ell(\sigma_t,\Upsilon_L))$) for any timelike geodesic $\sigma:[0,1] \to I(\Upsilon_{-R},\Upsilon_R)$, we have that
    \begin{equation}
        f_\delta'' \geq L_\mathsf g(\sigma)^2(1 {+} \delta f_\delta) \geq L_\mathsf g(\sigma)^2 (1 {+} \delta \mathrm{md}^{-\delta}(L-R)) = L_\mathsf g(\sigma)^2 \lambda.
    \end{equation}
    The same estimates work on the larger causally convex set $\{\ell(\Upsilon_{-L}, \cdot) > L - R\} \cap \{\ell(\cdot,\Upsilon_L) > L - R\} \cap I(\Upsilon_{-L},\Upsilon_L)$.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $(\mathcal M,\mathsf g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime, $C \subseteq \mathcal M$ an open and causally convex subset, and $f: C \rightarrow \mathbb R$ be a causally convex function. For $x \in C$ we define the \emph{causal subdifferential of $f$ at $x$} as the set
    \[
    \partial_\leq f(x) := \{ \omega \in  T^*_x \mathcal M 
    : f(x) + \omega[v] \leq f(\exp_x(v)) \; \forall \text{ causal } v \in \exp_x^{-1}(C)\}.
    \]

title: Proof
body_md:
If $x$ does not lie in the past causal cut locus of $y$, then this result holds with an equality instead of an inequality by the first variation formula, see \cite[p 264]{bookONeill}.
    If $x$ is in the past cut locus of $y$ then we have that $\sigma_s$ does not lie in the future cut locus of $x$ for $s \in [0,1)$. Hence we use reversed triangle inequality
    \[
    \ell(x, \gamma_t) \geq \ell( x, \sigma _s) + \ell(\sigma _s, \gamma_t).
    \]
    Now subtract on both sides $\ell(x, y)$ and use the fact that $\sigma$ is a maximizing geodesic to obtain
    \[
    \frac{\ell(x, \gamma_t) - \ell(x, y)}{t} \geq \frac{\ell(x, \sigma_s) + \ell(\sigma_s, \gamma_t) - \ell(x, y)}{t} = \frac{\ell(\sigma_s, \gamma_t) - \ell(\sigma_s, y) }{t}.
    \]
    Take the $\liminf$ in $t \rightarrow 0^+$, notice that the right-hand side is differentiable since $y$ is not in the future cut locus of $\sigma_s$ and $\gamma_t$ is right differentiable at $t= 0$, and {the first variation formula yields}    
    \begin{equation*}
    \liminf_{t \rightarrow 0^+} {\frac{\ell(x, \gamma_t) - \ell(x, y)}{t}} \geq  \frac{\mathsf g(-\exp_y^{-1} (\sigma_s),\gamma'_0)}{\mathsf g(-\exp_y^{-1} (\sigma_s), -\exp_y^{-1}(\sigma_s))^{1/2}}.
    \end{equation*}
    Letting $s \rightarrow 1^-$ on the right-hand side, the conclusion follows. The claim about $\ell(x,\gamma_t)^2$ easily follows from the above together with the chain rule.

label: lem: monotonicity 1
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: monotonicity 1}
    Let $x \in J(\Upsilon_{\tilde R}, \Upsilon_{R})$, where $-20 <\tilde R \leq R < 20$ and let $\gamma: [0,T] \rightarrow \mathcal M$ be the gradient flow of $\mathrm{md}^{-\delta}\circ F$ starting at $x$, and $[0,T]$ some compact subinterval in its maximal domain of existence. Then 
    \[
    \gamma_t \in J ( \Upsilon_{h_{\tilde R}(t)}, \Upsilon_{h_{R}(t)} ) 
    \]
    for all $t \in [0,T]$ such that $-20 \leq h_{\tilde R}(t) \leq h_{R}(t) \leq 20$. Analogously, if $\sigma :[0,T] \rightarrow \mathcal M$ is the gradient flow of $\mathrm{md}^{-\delta} \circ G$ starting at $x$, then 
    \[
    \sigma_t \in J ( \Upsilon_{-h_{-\tilde R}(t)}, \Upsilon_{-h_{-R}(t)} ) 
    \]
    for all $t \in [0,T]$ such that $-20 \leq -h_{-\tilde R}(t) \leq -h_{-R}(t) \leq 20$.

label: Proposition: Almost linearity
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Almost linearity of the Busemann functions along the flow

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma \ref{Lemma: Almost monotonicity of reparam grad flow}, the flow curves under consideration remain in
$I(\Upsilon_{-15},\Upsilon_{15})$ for $t\in[0,4]$.
We establish the following pointwise derivative estimates at
an arbitrary point $x\in I(\Upsilon_{-15},\Upsilon_{15})$.

    We proceed by bounding the right derivative $\frac{d}{dt}|^+_{t = 0} F(\bar \gamma_t)$ of $t \mapsto F(\bar \gamma_t)$ at $t = 0$. {The lower bound} is a consequence of $1$-steepness of $F$, {as we now show}:
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{d}{dt}\bigg|^+_{t = 0} F(\bar \gamma_t) \geq \frac{d}{dt}\bigg|^+_{t = 0} \ell(\bar \gamma_0,\bar \gamma_t) = g'(0) \frac{d}{dt}\bigg|^+_{t = 0} \ell(x, \gamma_t).
    \end{align*}
    Observe that the definition of gradient flow 
    {from Theorem \ref{Theorem: local existence}} and $1$-steepness of $F$ give
    \begin{align*}
        \ell(x,\gamma_t) \geq \int_{0}^t \|\dot \gamma_s\|_g \, ds \geq \int_0^t (\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})'(F(\gamma_s)) \, ds \geq t \, (\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})'(F(\gamma_0)).
    \end{align*}
    We conclude that
    \begin{equation*}
        \frac{d}{dt}\bigg|^+_{t = 0} \ell(x, \gamma_t) \geq (\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})'(F(x)).
    \end{equation*}
    Since $g'(0) = (\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})'(F(x))^{-1}$ by definition, it follows that
    \begin{equation*}
    \frac{d}{dt}\bigg|^+_{t = 0} F(\bar \gamma_t) \geq  1.
    \end{equation*}
    {Turning to the upper bound,} let $\eta:[0,F(x)] \to \mathcal M$ be a past directed maximizing $\mathsf g$-arclength parametrized timelike geodesic from $x$ to $\Upsilon_{-L}$. 

    It is possible to extend $\eta$ to a domain $[-1/4,F(x)]$, still
in $\mathsf g$-unit speed parametrization, such that
$\eta_{-1/4}\in I(\Upsilon_{-20},\Upsilon_{20})$.
To see this, smoothly extend $\eta$ by solving the geodesic equation
until its first intersection with $\partial J^-(\Upsilon_{20})$,
say at parameter $-\varepsilon$. Using triangle comparison for $\Delta(\Upsilon_{-L},\eta_{-\varepsilon},
\Upsilon_{20})$, together with the law of cosines, we obtain
\[
25 \le \ell(x,\Upsilon_{20})^2
\le \varepsilon\left[
\frac{(L+20)^2}{F(x)+\varepsilon}-F(x)
\right]+\Psi(\delta,L)
\le 80\varepsilon+\Psi(\delta,L)
\]
for sufficiently large $L$. Here $F(x)+\varepsilon$ is the length of the extended geodesic,
and the last inequality follows from $F(x)\ge L-15$. Thus $\varepsilon>1/4$. We now set $a:=1/1000$. Moreover, notice that
$\eta_a\in I(\Upsilon_{-20},\Upsilon_{20})$.
Indeed, the function
\[
f(t):=\operatorname{md}^{-\delta}
\bigl(\ell(\Upsilon_{-20},\eta_t)\bigr)
\]
is convex by Theorem \ref{Theorem: convexityoftimeseparation} as long as
$\eta_t\in I^+(\Upsilon_{-20})$. Since $x \in I(\Upsilon_{-15},\Upsilon_{15})$ and $\eta_{-1/4} \in I(\Upsilon_{-20},\Upsilon_{20})$, we can estimate
$f(0)\ge 25/2$ and $f(-1/4)\le 800+\Psi(\delta,L)$.
Using the convexity inequality at the points $-1/4,0,t$,
we therefore obtain
\[
f(t)\ge (1+4t)f(0)-4t f(-1/4)
\ge \frac{25}{2}-3150t-\Psi(\delta,L)>0
\qquad\text{for }0\le t\le a,
\]
provided $\delta,L^{-1}$ are small enough. Consequently,
$\eta_t$ cannot meet $\partial I^+(\Upsilon_{-20})$ in this
interval, and hence
$\eta([-a,a])\subset I(\Upsilon_{-20},\Upsilon_{20})$.
Restrict $\eta$ to $[-a,a]$. By convexity, the difference of right and left derivatives
can therefore be estimated as follows:
\begin{align*}
0 &\le
\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}^{+}
(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(F(\eta_s))
-
\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}^{-}
(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(F(\eta_s))
\\
&\le \frac{1}{a}\Big[
-2(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(F(x))
+(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(F(\eta_{-a}))
+(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(F(\eta_a))
\Big].
\end{align*}
Similarly, we obtain the analogous estimate for the difference
of right and left derivatives of
$(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(G(\eta_s))$:
\begin{align*}
0 &\le
\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}^{+}
(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(G(\eta_s))
-
\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}^{-}
(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(G(\eta_s))
\\
&\le \frac{1}{a}\Big[
-2(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(G(x))
+(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(G(\eta_{-a}))
+(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(G(\eta_a))
\Big].
\end{align*}
    Since $\eta$ is maximizing and unit speed from $x$ to $\Upsilon_{-L}$, we notice that
    \begin{align*}
     &\frac{d}{ds}\bigg|_{s = 0}^- (\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})(F(\eta_s)) = (\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})'(F(x)) \frac{d}{ds}\bigg|_{s = 0}^-F(\eta_s),
        \\&\frac{d}{ds}\bigg|_{s = 0}^+ (\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})(F(\eta_s)) = -(\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})'(F(x)).
    \end{align*}
It follows, by adding the nonnegative term involving $G$ to
the estimate for $F$, that
\begin{align*}
0 &\le
-(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})'(F(x))
\left(1+\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}^{-}F(\eta_s)\right)
\\
&\le \frac{1}{a}\Big[
-2\big[(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(F(x))
      +(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(G(x))\big]
\\
&\quad
+\big[(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(F(\eta_{-a}))
     +(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(G(\eta_{-a}))\big]
\\
&\quad
+\big[(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(F(\eta_a))
     +(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})(G(\eta_a))\big]
\Big].
\end{align*}
Expanding at this point the terms with
$\operatorname{md}^{-\delta}$ for small $\delta$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
0 &\le
-(\operatorname{md}^{-\delta})'(F(x))
\left(1+\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}^{-}F(\eta_s)\right)
\\
&\le \frac{1}{a}\Bigg[
-2\left(\frac{F(x)^2}{2}+\frac{G(x)^2}{2}\right)
\\
&\qquad\qquad
+\left(\frac{F(\eta_{-a})^2}{2}
      +\frac{G(\eta_{-a})^2}{2}\right)
+\left(\frac{F(\eta_a)^2}{2}
      +\frac{G(\eta_a)^2}{2}\right)
\Bigg]+\Psi.
\end{align*}
From Proposition \ref{Prop: Estimate on Busemann sum}, we know that
\[
-C\le L^2-\frac{F(z)^2}{2}-\frac{G(z)^2}{2}\le C
\qquad\text{for }z\in J(\Upsilon_{-20},\Upsilon_{20}),
\]
for some positive constant $C$ independent of $\delta,L$.
The expression in brackets is therefore bounded above by $4C$,
so the preceding right-hand side is bounded above by
$4C/a+\Psi$. Since $a$ is fixed, it follows that the difference
of right and left derivatives of
$\operatorname{md}^{-\delta}\circ F\circ\eta$ is bounded below
by $0$ and above by a constant independent of $\delta,L$. Thus, dividing by the large and growing term $(\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})'(F(x)) = F(x) + \Psi$, we obtain
    \begin{equation*}
        1 \leq {-} \frac{d}{ds}\bigg|_{s = 0}^-F(\eta_s) \leq 1 + \Psi.
    \end{equation*}
From here suppose that the properties $i)$ and $ii)$ of Theorem \ref{Theorem: local existence} hold at $t=0$. This assumption is allowed because it holds almost every time, and we will use it just to obtain an upper bound for the right derivative of $F(\overline{\gamma}_t)$, that we will integrate to obtain the conclusion. Let $v:= \dot \gamma_0$, hence $v^{\flat} \in \partial_\leq \, \mathrm{md}^{-\delta} \circ F(x)$. The defining properties of the gradient flow $\gamma_t$ and its reparameterization $\bar \gamma_t$, the fact that the geodesic $\eta_s$ is past directed and unit speed, and the reverse Cauchy--Schwarz inequality yields
\begin{equation*}
    (\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})' (F(x)) ( 1+ \Psi) \geq - \frac{d}{ds}\bigg|_{s = 0}^-\mathrm{md}^{-\delta} \circ F (\eta_s) \geq v^{\flat} [-\dot \eta_0] \geq \| v\|_{\mathsf g} \, ,
\end{equation*}
and, moreover, we have
\[
\| v\|_{\mathsf g} = (\mathrm{md}^{-\delta})' (F(x)) \, \sqrt{\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_{t = 0}^+ F(\bar \gamma_t)} \, .
\]
Hence, we get
    \begin{equation*}
        1 + \Psi \geq - \frac{d}{ds}\bigg|_{s = 0}^-F(\eta_s) \geq  \sqrt{\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_{t = 0}^+ F(\bar \gamma_t)}.
    \end{equation*}
    By arbitrariness of the point and uniqueness of gradient flows, these estimates hold {uniformly} for almost any $t \in [0,4]$, and the claim follows from the fundamental theorem of calculus.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $(\mathcal M,\mathsf g)$ be globally hyperbolic with timelike sectional
curvature bounded below by $-\delta\leq0$, and let
$\Upsilon:[-L,L]\to \mathcal M$ be a maximizing unit speed timelike
geodesic. Given $x\in H $ (where $H$ is as in \eqref{eq: H}), define
$t\mapsto\text{\rm Fl}^{+}_t(x)$ to be the reparametrized flow
$\bar\gamma_t=\gamma_{g(t)}$ of the function
$F=\ell(\Upsilon_{-L},\cdot)$, which in turn arises from the
gradient flow of the causally convex function
$\operatorname{md}^{-\delta}\circ F$ starting at $x$ and
maximal in $H$.
Similarly, we define $t\mapsto\text{\rm Fl}^{-}_t(x)$ as the
past-directed reparametrized flow of
$G=\ell(\cdot,\Upsilon_L)$, arising from the gradient flow of
$\operatorname{md}^{-\delta}\circ G$ maximal in $H$.
Both flow maps are defined on the respective maximal time
intervals of their reparametrizations.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $d$ be the minimal time such that
$\text{\rm Fl}^+_d(y)\ge x$, and set $q:=\text{\rm Fl}^+_d(y)$.
Then $\ell(x,q)^2=\ell_+(x,y)^2$.
Since $\text{\rm Fl}^-_s(x)\leq x\leq q$, the past almost
Pythagoras formula \eqref{past Pythagoras}, together with almost linearity \eqref{linearity},
gives
\begin{equation*}
\ell(\text{\rm Fl}^-_s(x),q)^2
=\ell_+(x,y)^2+s^2
+2s\bigl(b_L^+(x)-b_L^+(y)+d\bigr)+\Psi.
\end{equation*}
If $t\geq d$, we apply \eqref{future Pythagoras} to
$\text{\rm Fl}^-_s(x)\le q$, flowing $q$ forward for time
$t-d$. If $t<d$, we instead apply \eqref{future Pythagoras} to $\text{\rm Fl}^-_s(x)\leq\text{\rm Fl}^+_t(y)$, flowing the
second point forward for time $d-t$, and rearrange.
In both cases, almost linearity \eqref{linearity} yields
\begin{align*}
\ell(\text{\rm Fl}^-_s(x),\text{\rm Fl}^+_t(y))^2
&=\ell(\text{\rm Fl}^-_s(x),q)^2+(t-d)^2\\
&\quad+2(t-d)\bigl(b_L^+(x)-b_L^+(y)+d+s\bigr)+\Psi\\
&=\ell_+(x,y)^2+(t+s-d)^2\\
&\quad+2(t+s-d)\bigl(b_L^+(x)-b_L^+(y)+d\bigr)+\Psi,
\end{align*}
which proves \eqref{mixed Pythagoras}.

For $x,y\in X$, we have $b_L^+(x)=b_L^+(y)=0$ and
$\ell_+(x,y)=0$. Proposition \ref{P:almost symmetry} and \eqref{future Pythagoras} give
$\tilde{\mathsf d}(x,y)^2-d^2=\Psi$.
Since $\tilde{\mathsf d}(x,y)\ge d$, it follows that
$d=\tilde{\mathsf d}(x,y)+\Psi=\mathsf d(x,y)+\Psi$,
which proves \eqref{eq: pythagoras from slice}.
